title: af/storage-prune@3
description: `af storage prune --json` (ADR-0144): what one sweep removed, or without --apply would remove. A sweep plans once over one inventory snapshot and the applied sweep runs that plan entry by entry, never choosing again (ADR-0159 clause 13): first the deletions interruptions left (rule `recovery`), then collection (rule `collection`, and `keep_surveys` for the Surveys of a Project beyond `[storage] keep_surveys`), then the budget, least recently used first (rule `budget`), until the total fits `max_bytes` or nothing else may be removed (`stop`). Each removal says what it frees and af's total after it: as planned in a preview, as freed by the applied sweep. Gate cleanups of finished Tasks are those the sweep tried; registry entries whose path holds no Store any more are dropped; a failed removal is listed and tried again by the next sweep. Version 2 added the removal kind `survey` (ADR-0159 clause 13): a Survey's record in its Project Store's CAS, its `path` the CAS object, taken behind a `SurveyCollected@1` tombstone. A Survey whose record's bytes were no Survey is removed with `unreadable`, the reason its tombstone carries. The removals dead processes left claimed and the containers of dead Survey collections are in the one inventory snapshot and planned first (kind `claim`, rule `recovery`), a container that held a moved record after that record, so the preview lists exactly what the applied sweep removes; a claim inside a Project Store is counted once, in that Store's bytes. A registry entry whose path holds no Store is dropped by the plan (`registry_dropped`, the same in the preview and the applied sweep), after the inventory reached its parent's claims. A planned entry of any kind whose removal failed (the lock lost, what it names replaced or gone since inventory, an I/O error) keeps its place in the applied sweep's removals with `outcome` `failed: <reason>` and nothing freed (`bytes` 0, the total after it unchanged), unless a deletion stopped part way (its walk could not reach or unlink everything, or its final `rmdir` failed): its `bytes` are then what left the disk, what the directory held when its removal started, stated immediately before anything was unlinked, less what its claim still holds. Version 3 makes the running total reconcile what it cannot have known: a removal that measured what its entry held when it started puts those bytes in place of the inventory's before what left the disk is taken out, so a claim that grew since inventory and was removed part way leaves exactly what it still holds in the total; and when what a deletion that stopped part way left cannot be measured, the total after it and after the sweep is `unknown`, and so is `stop`, never `fits`. Every `bytes` is the allocated bytes of the regular files an entry holds or a removal deleted: directories and links count nothing, on every file system. What the plan leaves is listed under `left`, by the preview and the applied sweep alike, with its reason: `held` (its Project Store's `project.lock` cannot be taken now), `foreign` (a file at a collected Survey's CAS name after its record was moved, or anything under `cas/removing` that is no collected Survey's record; never deleted, and counted in its Project Store's bytes, never a Survey's), `oversize` (a record over 1 MiB), `unreadable_name` (a name under `cas/removing` that is not UTF-8, a file's or its container's), `too_deep` (a directory entry or claim nested deeper than the removal walk's 128 levels, which no removal could take whole: listed in use by `af storage`, never removed) or `unmeasurable` (a claim a dead process left whose walk could not measure it: it holds no bytes the plan could account for, so it is never planned). A Survey whose record cannot be reached without a link or read is a failure, and keeps its record and its place in the log.

total_after.description: af's total after the sweep: as planned in a preview; after what the applied sweep freed, or `unknown` once a removal stopped part way and what it left cannot be measured.

stop.description: `fits`: the total fits the budget; `nothing_evictable`: still over it, and the rest is in use or was used within the hour; `unknown`: the total is unknown, so neither is claimed.

total_after.description: af's total after this removal: as planned in a preview, after what the applied sweep freed, or `unknown` from a removal on that stopped part way and could not measure what it left.

unreadable.description: A `survey` removal only: why its record's bytes were no Survey, as its `SurveyCollected@1` tombstone says.

outcome.description: The applied sweep, any kind: `failed: <reason>` when its removal failed, so it freed nothing (`bytes` 0) and `total_after` is the total before it, unless a deletion stopped part way and `bytes` is what left the disk; the next sweep plans again.

left.description: What the plan leaves where it is (ADR-0159 clause 13), by the preview and the applied sweep alike. The next pass plans again.

path.description: The path as it is when it is UTF-8; otherwise in the canonical percent-encoded spelling of `review_core::encode_path`, with `path_encoded`.
